summary: The design fits the existing guardrail architecture, but several contracts are underspecified or currently incompatible: transformed content cannot carry a report, RAG context bypasses TOOL_OUTPUT, output checks lack the rendered prompt, and synchronous inference runs inside async checks. The highest risks are content leakage through existing security logging, incomplete streaming protection, and an insufficiently reproducible model bake-off.

suggestions.title: Make reports orthogonal to actions
suggestions.rationale: `GuardrailResult` has one action, while `GuardrailPipeline` only accumulates reports for FLAG/BLOCK. `PromptInjectionGuardrail` returns TRANSFORM without a report, yet the proposed TOOL_OUTPUT behavior requires TRANSFORM plus FLAG. Add an independent report-attachment path and test that transformed INPUT and TOOL_OUTPUT content still produces metadata without offending text.

suggestions.title: Close the existing content-leaking telemetry path
suggestions.rationale: `SecurityEventLogger` logs `matched_text` and can persist `original_input` and `sanitized_input`. That contradicts the stated content-free telemetry invariant and would be especially dangerous for prompt-leakage detections. Define a content-free security event payload containing only category, severity, score, counts, and bounded metadata, then test both logger output and database arguments.

suggestions.title: Remove synchronous inference from async checks
suggestions.rationale: `PromptInjectionGuardrail.check()` calls `engine.score()` synchronously; only warmup uses `asyncio.to_thread`. Adding a jailbreak model, embedding lookup, and fuzzy matching can block the event loop on every request. Offload inference and expensive matching through a bounded execution strategy, retain ORT thread caps, and benchmark event-loop latency under concurrent requests.

suggestions.title: Add an explicit RAG-content scanning seam
suggestions.rationale: The TOOL_OUTPUT hook routes string `ToolResult` fields through the pipeline, but non-string fields bypass `check()`, and retrieved vector content is assembled directly into `vector_context` before `create_system_prompt()`. Therefore `scan_tool_output=True` does not cover all poisoned RAG chunks. Scan individual retrieved chunks before concatenation, or define a separate retrieval-content stage with clear structured-value semantics.

suggestions.title: Capture the exact rendered system prompt per turn
suggestions.rationale: `AbstractBot.system_prompt` exposes a template, while `create_system_prompt()` adds dynamic memory, retrieval, metadata, skills, and output-mode layers. `_run_output_pipeline()` currently passes only the AI message, so leakage detection cannot reliably compare against the prompt actually sent to the provider. Capture the final rendered artifact at each invoke/ask/stream seam and pass it through request-local context; do not re-render at OUTPUT time.

suggestions.title: Make streaming leakage limits explicit
suggestions.rationale: `ask_stream()` emits chunks before the final OUTPUT pipeline runs. The existing `StreamingGuardrail` contract can buffer content, but the ordinary OUTPUT guardrail cannot retract already-emitted leaked chunks. Either ship prompt leakage as final-message-only detection with explicit documentation and telemetry, or implement a bounded buffering adapter before enabling blocking semantics.

suggestions.title: Define stage-specific ordering
suggestions.rationale: `Guardrail` has one scalar priority and pipelines sort only by that value. The proposed leakage guardrail needs different INPUT and OUTPUT bands, while SecretsGuardrail and PromptInjectionGuardrail both use priority 10, making TOOL_OUTPUT order depend on registration order. Add per-stage priority or separate stage adapters and test deterministic transform/block ordering.

suggestions.title: Keep classifier and embedding engines as explicit backends
suggestions.rationale: The current ONNX engine assumes tokenizer files, logits, and `id2label`, while the benchmark embedding detector requires vector encoding and a reference matrix. A shared `score(text)` protocol alone does not capture loading, artifact validation, corpus ownership, or warmup. Use an explicit engine descriptor/backend interface with category-scoped caches, preserving the existing injection resolver and compatibility behavior.

suggestions.title: Turn the bake-off into a hard reproducible gate
suggestions.rationale: `compare_models.py` currently uses a small hardcoded sample set and a fixed 0.5 threshold, while `corpus.py` contains richer held-out buckets and a disjoint embedding seed corpus. Extend the gate with per-category corpora, Spanish-benign minimums, threshold selection, p50/p95 latency, startup/memory measurements, classifier parity, and a candidate license/model manifest. Do not pin a default until these artifacts are committed and the gate fails closed.

suggestions.title: Require provenance before shipping embedding artifacts
suggestions.rationale: The proposed 0din candidate has no declared license, and the repository’s embedding benchmark ships attack seed text directly in `corpus.py`. Derived vectors or packaged attack corpora need explicit redistribution rights, versioning, integrity hashes, and bounded memory requirements. Treat an uncleared candidate as non-default and require an offline, versioned artifact manifest.

suggestions.title: Avoid making rapidfuzz a core dependency by default
suggestions.rationale: `rapidfuzz` is currently declared only in the optional `graphindex` extra, while prompt leakage runs on the core guardrail path. Benchmark `difflib.SequenceMatcher` against an optional rapidfuzz backend and make the matcher injectable; if rapidfuzz becomes mandatory, update the core dependency and minimal-install boundary deliberately.
